# Interfacing an LED with Arduino Uno&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

# Aim

To interface a light-emitting diode (LED) with an Arduino Uno microcontroller board and execute an embedded C++ program to toggle the LED between ON and OFF states at regular time intervals.

&nbsp;

## Components

![][image1]

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

WORKING

&nbsp;

## Working Principle

1. The circuit forms a closed electrical loop with the Arduino acting as a digitally controlled DC voltage source.  
2. A current-limiting resistor (220 Ω) is placed in series with the LED to prevent excessive current draw from the microcontroller pin, protecting both the pin and the diode from burnout.  
3. During execution, the microcontroller configures Digital Pin 13 as a digital output via the `pinMode()` function.  
4. Setting the pin to `HIGH` provides a 5 V potential difference across the circuit, forward-biasing the LED and allowing current to flow so it illuminates.  
5. Setting the pin to `LOW` drops the output voltage to 0 V (ground reference), terminating current flow and turning the LED off.  
6. Time delays between state transitions are controlled via the `delay()` routine, which blocks execution for the specified number of millisecond

#### SCHEMATIC DIAGRAM

&nbsp;

![][image3]

&nbsp;

CODE

&nbsp;

int trig \= 9;

int echo \= 10;

&nbsp;

void setup() {

&nbsp;&nbsp;Serial.begin(9600);

&nbsp;&nbsp;pinMode(trig, OUTPUT);

&nbsp;&nbsp;pinMode(echo, INPUT);

}

&nbsp;

void loop() {

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;digitalWrite(trig, HIGH);

&nbsp;&nbsp;delayMicroseconds(10);

&nbsp;&nbsp;digitalWrite(trig, LOW);

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;long result \= pulseIn(echo, HIGH);

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;Serial.println(result);

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;delay(1000);

}

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

##### Applications

* **Visual Status Indicators:** Provides real-time power and operational state feedback in electronic appliances and embedded systems.  
* **Warning and Hazard Lights:** Used in roadside signaling devices, tower obstruction markers, and emergency vehicle flashers.  
* **Automotive Directional Signals:** Drives the flashing sequence for vehicle turn signals and emergency hazard indicators.  
* **Hardware Diagnostics:** Encodes system operational states and hardware error codes via timed blink sequences on embedded circuit boards.

![][image4]

The LED connected to Digital Pin 13 turned ON and OFF alternately with an interval of 1 second, confirming successful hardware interfacing and program execution on the Arduino Uno.
